scenes.title: What happened, what changed
scenes.subtitle: From one request to a published video library
scenes.say: Here is what happened in this build, and what changed along the way.

scenes.title: The ask
items: One library every agent uses for videos
The same voice and look every time
Narration without having to ask for it
Fast, even on a CPU-only cloud machine
scenes.say: The ask was simple. Build one library that every agent reaches for when it needs a video. The same voice and look every time. Narration without having to ask for it. And fast, even on a cloud machine with no GPU.

scenes.title: What got built
items: A JSON spec: scenes, each with a line to say
A local voice, cached sentence by sentence
Scenes timed to the real audio, captions included
check, preview, render and record commands
scenes.say: Here is what got built. A JSON spec, where every scene has a line to say. A local voice, cached one sentence at a time. Scenes timed to the real audio, with captions. And four commands: check, preview, render, and record.

scenes.title: Eleven scene types
scenes.subtitle: The one-second preview shows every scene before rendering
scenes.say: There are eleven scene types, from title cards to code, stats, and before and after comparisons. The preview command shows all of them on one image in about a second.

scenes.title: The speed fix

left.title: First version
items: Every frame drawn and encoded
Parallel encoders fought for the CPU
160 seconds for an 87-second video

right.title: Frame holding
items: Only frames that change are drawn
Repeats happen inside ffmpeg, almost free
35 seconds for the same video

scenes.say: The biggest change was speed. The first version drew and encoded every single frame, and its parallel encoders fought over the CPU. It took a hundred and sixty seconds for an eighty seven second video. Now, only frames that actually change are drawn, and repeats are made inside ffmpeg, almost for free. The same video takes thirty five seconds.

scenes.label: faster renders on a laptop CPU, with no GPU
scenes.say: That is about four and a half times faster, on a laptop CPU, with no GPU.

scenes.title: Added on request
scenes.subtitle: TikTok captions · GIFs in and out · fonts · screen recording
scenes.say: Then came the requests. TikTok style videos, with big word by word captions. GIFs in and out. Custom fonts. And screen recording, for game trailers.

scenes.title: Bugs caught on the way
items: The voice crashed inside worker threads, so it moved to processes
The report file overwrote the spec, so it was renamed
Captions merged two sentences, so the splitter was fixed
scenes.say: A few bugs were caught on the way. The voice engine crashed inside worker threads, so it moved to separate processes. The render report overwrote the spec file, so it got a new name. And captions merged two sentences, so the sentence splitter was fixed.

scenes.title: The rename

left.title: narrated
items: Named after one feature
Easy to miss when searching

right.title: makevideo
items: Matches how people ask
Reads like a sentence: npx makevideo

scenes.say: And the name changed. narrated described just one feature. makevideo matches how people actually ask for a video, and the command reads like a sentence.

scenes.title: Decisions for you
items: Publish to npm? It needs your npm login
Install the agent skill for all your projects?
Next speed target: the voice, which is still the slowest step
scenes.say: Three decisions for you. Should it be published to npm? That needs your login. Should the agent skill be installed for all your projects? And should the next round focus on the voice, which is still the slowest step?

scenes.title: makevideo
scenes.subtitle: github.com/random00000000/makevideo
scenes.say: That is makevideo, version zero point one.
